elements.element: Audit no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company" (existing text retained)

elements.element: Conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality
elements.evidence: "by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality"

elements.element: Vendor bears audit cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" — unconditional Vendor cost, more favourable to Customer than the 5% carve-out

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "shall not include any direct access to the Company's systems"
"no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "fees incurred by HDI ... shall be borne by HDI"

reasons: All preferred elements are satisfied: once-per-12-months cap, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent confidentiality-bound auditor, no direct system access, and Vendor-borne cost (unconditional, which is better for us than the 5% carve-out).

The insertion adds "off-site where possible", a protection not required by either level; it duplicates/extends the no-direct-access limit and is not needed to complete the preferred position, so minimality fails on that short phrase only.
No undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics are introduced; the existing notice, business-hours and cost-allocation terms remain effective.
